gaps.note: THE SOURCE IS CLEAR AND THE LIBRARY IS SHORT: BK at 4x shows the rear's Config. Port as a female DE-9 (nine socket holes in a grey insert), and the vendor is not silent about it. What is missing is a part - the library has only the male half (std/db9@1, composed by common/db9-receptacle@1) - so it is drawn male. Its place, size and standoffs are right; its gender is not. The reason is the nearest the vocabulary has; none names a missing library part.
gaps.wanted: a female DE-9 receptacle part (sockets in a flush insert, as std/vga@1 draws its own), to replace the male one here.

gaps.note: the owner's manual says each outlet LED illuminates when its outlet is live and names no colour; the spec sheet says "power on-off status" and names none; every photograph shows the lamps unlit. The `on` state is declared with no colour, so the kit paints its default lit colour.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a powered PDUMH20NET, or Tripp Lite's word on the lamp colour.

gaps.note: the sides carry the tapped holes the mounting brackets screw to (three #6-32 screws a bracket, at more than one depth: owner's manual 1-1 and Features), and _C and DT02 show some of them, but only at a steep angle; no straight view or drawing of a side exists, so the sides are drawn bare.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of a side with a scale, or a dimensioned drawing.

gaps.note: no source shows the top or the bottom straight on: the spec sheet and the owner's manual have no such view, _C and DT02 see the lid only at a steep angle (a plain black lid with small screws near its edges), and nothing shows the underside. Both faces are drawn bare.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the top and the bottom with a scale.

gaps.note: no photograph or drawing shows the PDU with the WEBCARDLX out, so the slot's hole is not measured. The bay states the plate's main body, 67.3 by 29.1, as its opening: the largest hole the plate covers, an upper bound.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the PDU with the card removed, or the slot's dimensions from Tripp Lite.

gaps.note: no held source dimensions the WEBCARDLX behind its faceplate or the slot it sits in (the WEBCARDLX manual gives none), so the card states no depth.
gaps.wanted: the WEBCARDLX's dimensions from Tripp Lite.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `power` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 1 bay (front 1) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

capability.note: datasheet - the spec sheet sells it as a switched PDU ("PDU Type: Switched"; "16 individually switched output receptacles"), and what it meters is the input: "Network interface provides PDU control and data regarding input voltage and total output load level in amps"; "Digital display continuously reports total output load level in amps". No bank or outlet is metered. So `metering-scope: input` and `outlet-switching: true`, the class `switched-metered-input` (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 2.2, which names this PDU). Every outlet declares `[on, off]` on its own placement, not on the group, so the outlets stay slots a cord end can be seated in.

card.note: datasheet - the WEBCARDLX is eaton/webcardlx@1 in a bay, as the G4 eNMC is (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 7): the spec sheet calls it "Pre-installed", and the WEBCARDLX manual installs the same card in a UPS or a PDU. The bay is the card plate's envelope, tabs included (289.6, 4.4, 85.8 by 29.1). THE HOLE BEHIND THE PLATE IS NOT SEEN in any photograph: its `opening` is stated as the plate's main body, 67.3 by 29.1, the largest hole the plate can cover, so the tabs' corners stay metal. It is an upper bound and not a measurement (gaps: card-opening).

chassis.note: datasheet - spec sheet Unit Dimensions (hwd) 1.750 x 17.500 x 15.500 in, 4.44 x 44.4 x 39.4 cm; 1U (Rack Height); unit weight 12.50 lb, 5.67 kg; minimum rack depth 20.5 in. Material of construction: metal. Colour photo-measured: the face's median is #1d1d1b in DT01 (1653 px below outlet 6) and #1b1a18 in BK (9605 px right of the cord).

config-port.note: KNOWN WRONG IN ONE RESPECT: THE PORT IS A FEMALE DE-9 AND IS DRAWN MALE. BK at 4x shows nine dark socket holes in a grey insert, five over four, with a hex jackscrew standoff each side; the library's only DE-9 (common/db9-receptacle@1 over std/db9@1) draws the male half, pins standing in a recessed insert (gaps: female-de9). Its position and size are measured. The rear prints "Config. Port"; the owner's manual (Features) calls it the Factory Port, "reserved for configuration by factory authorized personnel only. Do not connect anything to the port." So it is not exported as a console.

dcim.note: the input is the cord, one `nema-l5-20p` power port (eaton/tripplite-cord-l5-20p@1), and each outlet a `nema-5-20r` power outlet fed by it (both types in NetBox and Nautobot, dcim/choices.py at the commits dcim_export.py cites). THE OUTLETS ARE NAMED AS THE UNIT PRINTS THEM, 1 to 16: the `interfaces:` rule maps each `outlet-<n>` to its numeral. No source names a breaker for this model (the spec sheet and the manual mention none), so no outlet runs `through` one. NO feed_leg IS WRITTEN: a single-phase PDU is on whatever leg its plug is on (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 5.2). The card's ports export on its module type (eaton/webcardlx@1 says how); the factory DE-9 is not a console and exports nothing.

ears.note: NOT DRAWN: THE EARS ARE SEPARATE BRACKETS, so the face is the 444 body and the generic ear stands for them (`chassis.ears`). DT01, BK and _C show a body with no flange at either end; DT02 shows the kit beside it - two long brackets with a flange at one end and two short square ones - and the owner's manual (Installation, 1-1) has the two longer brackets screwed to the sides with three #6-32 screws each for 1U rack mounting, "in a recessed position by attaching the mounting brackets so they extend beyond the front panel". The short ones are for 0U, wall and under-counter mounting (1-2 to 1-4). The spec sheet: "Mounting ears are reversible for front or rear facing rackmount installation". So three positions are named and none is dimensioned: flush (the manual's 1-1 figure, the default), recessed (1-1's text) and rear (the spec sheet). The brackets are black: DT02's short brackets read #1b1a16 (8400 px), the lit long bracket #33312b (24000 px).

front.note: photo-measured - DT01, mm from the face's left and top. Eight 5-20R outlets, numbered 8 to 1 left to right as printed, their square faces 27 across (the part's) with their tops at 5.6 and their centres at 18.1 and then every 35.95, the pitch common to both faces (see `rear`); read alone, this face's outlet edges give 36.1, its numerals 36.06 and its lamps 36.02, and the bow (see `method`) leaves the fit's residuals within 0.9. Each is turned 90 degrees, so its U earth hole is on the right with its round side toward the slots, the plain line slot at the top left and the T neutral slot below it, as DT01 shows. Under each, its numeral (bold white, about 3.1 high, baseline 36.7) and below that a round lamp at 39.6, about 1.8 across, so common/led-dot@1. A hole about 3 across at (7.6, 39.3), below outlet 8. The WEBCARDLX's faceplate from 289.6 to 375.4 across and 4.4 to 33.5 down (its own provenance has the detail), and the load meter's bezel from 387.8 to 413.1 across and 10.65 to 29.2 down, with LOAD (AMPS) centred under it (read at 399.8) on a baseline at 32.4, about 1.9 high.

ground.note: photo-measured and datasheet - the spec sheet's Grounding: "Grounding lug". BK shows a Phillips screw on a toothed washer, the washer about 12 across; common/ground-screw-washer@1 (11.0, a pan head on its washer) is the library's part of that kind and size. The earth symbol beside it is printed without a circle, so it is drawn as silkscreen and not as common/ground-symbol@1.

holes.note: the three holes, about 3 across, near the bottom edge (one on the front, two on the rear) are drawn as holes; nothing held names them. The manual fixes the cord retention shelf to "the front panel of the PDU" with two #6-32 screws (1-5), which they may take, but no figure shows where.

input.note: datasheet - spec sheet INPUT: single-phase, 120 V, recommended service single-phase 20 A 120 V, maximum input 16 A ("Agency de-rated to 16A continuous"), plug NEMA 5-20P; NEMA L5-20P, cord 12 ft (3.66 m); OUTPUT 1.92 kW (120 V) / 16 A total, 50/60 Hz. The cord is fixed (manual, Features: "permanently attached"), so `input-plug` is the slug the cord exports, `nema-l5-20p`, and the 5-20P is the adapter in the box. It leaves the rear face through a bushing 107.3 to 127.1 across, the left of centre seen from behind (COVERAGE: "the rear left").

lamps.note: datasheet and photo - the spec sheet: "16 LEDs display power on-off status for each output receptacle"; the owner's manual (2-3): "The LED B near each output receptacle illuminates when the receptacle is ready to distribute live AC power". Each is common/led-dot@1 under its outlet's numeral, placed with `for:` naming the outlet so a state set on the outlet reaches its lamp (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2). The `outlet-leds` group declares `on` lit and `off` unlit, and NO COLOUR, because no held source states one (gaps: outlet-lamp-colour); every photograph shows them unlit.

logo.note: the rear prints Eaton's stylised wordmark; it is not drawn, and the area it covers is the `logo-zone` region. The front prints no wordmark.

meter.note: photo and datasheet - eaton/tripplite-ammeter@1, its bezel at (387.8, 10.65); the spec sheet: "Digital display continuously reports total output load level in amps". It is not the 0U strip's meter: no button, no decimal points, and nothing says it turns over.

method.note: NO DRAWING EXISTS, SO EVERY POSITION IS READ OFF THE TWO STRAIGHT-ON EATON PHOTOGRAPHS. Searched: the spec sheet, the Eaton SKU export, the owner's manual (933687 rev A) and the WEBCARDLX manual dimension nothing on the faces, and no submittal drawing is published (the address the PDUMV20HVNETLX's follows returns 404). PDUMH20NET_DT01 (front) and PDUMH20NET_BK (rear) are 3000 px masters, each spanning the PDU's 444 mm (the spec sheet's 17.5 in, 44.4 cm) in 2520 px: 5.676 px per mm across. Each face is about 251 px high against the spec sheet's 44.4 mm, 5.65 px per mm, so the two axes agree within half a percent at the middle. THE PHOTOGRAPHS ARE NOT QUITE ORTHOGRAPHIC: DT01's face tapers from 252 px high at its left end to 248 at its right, and the repeated features bow by about 1 mm at mid-length against a straight-line fit (about 0.5 mm on BK, which is also turned 0.18 degrees, 8 px over its length, and was read against its local top edge). THE SCALE IS PROVED BY TWO FEATURES OF KNOWN SIZE, independent of the body: the rear DE-9's jackscrew standoffs sit 25.1 apart against the 24.99 of the D-subminiature shell (TE C-747905), and the outlets' square faces read 27.0 to 27.6 across (mean 27.3, six read) against the 27.0 of the NEMA 5-20R face std/nema-5-20r@1 carries, so the scale holds within about one percent. Edges are soft and the faces bow, so a position is good to about 0.5 mm near the ends and about 1 mm at mid-length, not better. THE OUTLET PITCH IS UNIFORM ON PURPOSE: the bow is the camera's and not the hardware's, so a straight-line fit is drawn rather than each outlet where the photograph puts it.

outlets.note: datasheet and photo - the spec sheet: "16 switched NEMA 5-15/20R outlets (8 front / 8 rear)", 16 A total and 16 A max per outlet; the owner's manual (Features) draws the 5-15/20R face with its T slot. Each is std/nema-5-20r@1, the 27 mm face the photographs measure. Numbered as printed: 1 to 8 on the front, 9 to 16 on the rear, each face numbered from its right as seen.

rear.note: photo-measured - BK, mm from the rear face's left (the PDU's right end seen from behind) and top. At the left: the ground screw on its star washer, 12 across, centred (10.0, 11.2), with an earth symbol printed right of it (17.2 to 21.2 across, 7.6 to 12.0 down: the unit prints it about 1.4 above the screw's centre, which L61 notes and the baseline carries); the DE-9 with its two jackscrew standoffs centred (15.8, 28.2) and (40.9, 28.2), its wide row up, and "Config. Port" centred under it at 28.7, baseline 39.0; the Eaton wordmark from 51.3 to 98.5 across and 16.4 to 28.2 down; and the cord's bushing from 107.3 to 127.1 across. Then eight outlets numbered 16 to 9 left to right, faces 27 across centred at 174.5 and every 35.95 (read alone, their edges give 36.03 and their lamps 35.88), turned 90 as on the front, their tops at 4.4; numerals on a baseline at 36.4; lamps at 39.3. Holes about 3 across at (121.1, 38.6) and (436.1, 39.4). THE REAR OUTLETS SIT ABOUT 1.2 HIGHER than the front ones: the faces' top edges read 4.6 against 5.5, the line slots' lit edges 10.4 against 11.8 and the T slots' 28.1 against 29.7, each read at three outlets on each face, while the numerals and lamps of the two faces agree within 0.3. It is drawn as measured. THE OUTLETS STAND BACK TO BACK, so both faces take one pitch: a least-squares fit of the sixteen lamps with one pitch and an offset per face gives 35.94, drawn 35.95, and puts outlet 9's centre 17.85 and outlet 8's 18.1 from the PDU's left end seen from the front.
